deliverable.title: Hackathon Quick Start: A Developer's Guide
deliverable.body:
# Hackathon Quick Start: A Developer's Guide

## 1. Generate Content
Open the `/start` directory and edit `tools/facts.mjs` to customize the data. After making your changes, run the following command to dynamically update the pages:
```bash
node tools/gen.mjs
```

## 2. Customise Design
To modify the layout and design, edit `tools/designs.mjs`. Once you’ve made your adjustments, refresh the `/start` page to see the changes reflected.

## 3. Deploy Changes
Push your edits to the GitHub repository. The workflows will handle the deployment automatically, and no additional credentials are required.

---

deliverable.title: First Ten Minutes with Mistral
deliverable.body:
Three things to try in your first ten minutes [1]:

1. Make a first call to a Mistral model in five minutes. Open / (the home page, the hackathon briefing) [1]. No key at all: install Ollama, pull ministral-3:3b, and curl http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions [3]. Or with your own Mistral key: get a key from the Mistral console, export MISTRAL_API_KEY, and curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/chat/completions with model ministral-3b-2512 [2][3].

2. Open the demos and run the same brief on Mistral beside another model [2]. Open /demos/side-by-side.html: the local brain needs no key, while the Mistral and OpenRouter brains use their own keys, each sent only to its own provider [4]. /demos/on-device.html needs no key at all [4].

3. Open /team/: replay a recorded run with no key at all, or give a brief that needs your own Mistral key [4]. Or open /swarm/run.html to run the swarm on your own Mistral key [4].
